_comment: Example config for plotting/plot_sequence_eval.py (sequence-eval success by
task position and by task, as bars).   Schema: plotting/plot_common.py.
python plotting/plot_sequence_eval.py --config plotting/configs/plot_sequence_example.json
Paths point at a STANDALONE EVAL's glob dir -- the one holding
eval_per_trial.csv -- not at the training run. scripts/eval.sh puts it
next to the checkpoint it evaluates:
<TRAIN_RUN>/wandb/run-<ts>-<id>/eval/wandb/run-<ts2>-<id2>/glob
(or under $RUN_OUT_DIR when that is set). Training glob dirs have no
eval_per_trial.csv and are skipped with a [warn].
Each entry in `groups` is one bar colour. The pooled figures hold one
domain each and are drawn solid; a per-task figure holds both in one
bar, aligned: out-of-domain solid, in-domain hatched (///) over it.
Each entry in a group's `runs` is one series
(typically the eval of one seed's checkpoint); the bar is the mean
across them. A `runs` entry that is a LIST is several round shards of ONE
eval (e.g. --eval-rounds 0-2 and 3-5 run on two GPUs), pooled into one
series (a trial two shards both ran is averaged) -- or merge them first
with tools/rebuild_eval_outputs.py.
Writes to `out_dir` (empty = next to this file):
<name>_seq_position_<metric>_<kind>_<domain>.png   pooled over tasks
<name>_seq_position_<metric>_<kind>_per_task/...   one PNG per task
<name>_seq_position.csv                     every plotted number
<name>_seq_task_<metric>_<kind>.png    x = task, position pooled away
<name>_seq_task_<metric>_<kind>_per_scene/...  --per-scene, one PNG
per scene (CSV `group`)
<name>_seq_task.csv               the same numbers, `scene=__all__`
for the pooled-over-scenes bars
The _seq_task figures are the plain per-task success rate over every
position the task was met at; they are written on every run, and
--per-scene (a flag, not a config key) adds the per-scene split.
metric:   one or a list of: success (each task on its own) |
success_chained (a failed task fails every later one) |
grasp | obj_grasped -- one figure set per metric
seq_kind: each (default: seen and unseen orders get their own figures)
| pooled (averaged together) | seen/training | unseen/random
<kind> in the filenames is seen | unseen (recorded as
training | random -- the orders training ran, and the rest)
Both can be overridden on the command line (--metric, --seq-kind).
Any top-level key starting with '_' is ignored, so this block can stay.
